prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: automated hospital medication dispensing/returns; goals timeliness, pharmacist oversight, traceability. Aliases: Medication Order Gateway=Morrowglass; Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot=Cinderwake; Pharmacy Verification Station=Juniper; Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler=Bluejay; Medication Return Kiosk=Tallowmere; Registered Nurse=Larkspur; Pharmacy Technician=Copperfield; Biomedical Engineer=Stonewake. Elements: Medication Order Gateway validates orders from authorized clinical systems, flags bad data, routes to pharmacy review, gives order status, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Pharmacy Verification Station does final check, blocks release while incomplete, produces Batch Release Note. Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot prepares orders, presents package at Verification Station, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag; North Ward Cabinet Controller uses it to confirm ward before tote acceptance. Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler keeps range, records/displays temps and excursions, reports connectivity loss. East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles route via Pneumatic Tube Network; East checks route availability, monitors capsules, sends Tube Route Exception Ticket. Network admits only compliant loads after package IDs/destination reconciled with load info. North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers record arrival time/destination cabinet for own ward, report availability, block dispensing when Out of Service. Medication Return Kiosk guides return-bin checks, records outcomes, produces Return Bin Audit Label; Pharmacy Technician uses it to identify bins for collection. Actors: Clinical Pharmacist approves orders, reviews exceptions, produces Dose Exception Review Slip. Pharmacy Technician preps, confirms contents/IDs, checks cooler, verifies capsules, produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. Medication Safety Officer produces Diversion Review Packet. Registered Nurse confirms need, verifies load intended for ward, checks refrigerated handling, confirms return eligibility/segregation from waste. Charge Nurse sends Cabinet Downtime Notice. Hospital Courier checks handoff, records acceptance, produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record. Biomedical Engineer inspects hardware. IT Operations Specialist checks connectivity/logs. Rules: discrepancies block prep; release checked vs approved instructions, linked to order/package ID, time, credentials; canceled/duplicate held; manifest before network entry; route/packaging problem holds load until resolved/documented; receipt check (packaging, legible IDs vs task list, quantity/descriptions, temperature) before cabinet placement; mismatched loads isolated, never in active stock; accepted stock staged until placement authorized; receipt/discrepancies recorded; return bins checked intact/clean/correct stream, close securely; excursion stock/returns segregated. Modes: normal routing; manual/alternate delivery with staff

New part:
S118: Staff reconcile the bin contents with the return entry before the bin is closed.
S119: Questionable or damaged returned medication is segregated and referred for review rather than combined with accepted returns.
S120: A checked return bin remains secured in its designated holding location until collection is authorized.
S121: The Hospital Courier collects only bins that are closed and recorded as ready for collection.
S122: The Charge Nurse ensures that unresolved receipt or return discrepancies remain assigned for follow-up at shift handover.
S123: A dose exception is any mismatch, omission, duplicate request, or clinically implausible value detected before a medication is released for use.
S124: The affected transaction remains on hold until an authorized reviewer documents a disposition.
S125: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot stops the affected pick sequence and keeps the package in a controlled hold location pending review.
S126: Cinderwake preserves the scanned product and quantity data associated with the exception.
S127: Juniper compares the active order with the scanned product, strength, and measured quantity, and blocks verification when a field differs.
S128: Pharmacy Verification Station uses the review slip to record the exception category, evidence checked, disposition, and reviewer identity.
S129: The Clinical Pharmacist assesses dose, route, timing, and patient-specific clinical concerns before approving a correction or rejecting the order.
S130: A correction requires a valid authorized order and must not be inferred from prior dispensing history.
S131: Larkspur keeps the cabinet transaction locked and confirms that the medication has not been administered while review is pending.
S132: The Registered Nurse escalates an urgent patient-care concern to the Clinical Pharmacist and follows the hospital's clinical response procedure.
S133: The Registered Nurse does not bypass a hold or substitute a product to clear an exception.
S134: The Charge Nurse assigns unresolved exceptions to a named role and confirms that ownership is maintained at shift handover.
S135: The Pharmacy Technician may gather package and transaction evidence but may not make a clinical dose decision.
S136: The Medication Order Gateway rejects incomplete or internally inconsistent order updates and retains the rejection reason for review.
S137: The North Ward Cabinet Controller prevents access to a held transaction until an authorized disposition is recorded.
S138: The South Ward Cabinet Controller reports a failed lock or an unrecognized access attempt for immediate operational review.
S139: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler reports excursions that could affect medication suitability, and affected stock remains unavailable pending assessment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
